checks.name: capture-spread-interval-derivation
checks.summary: A8's derivation, recomputed in code from the declared numbers so a weight change cannot leave the interval stale. Let D be the seconds by which the flood's capture time precedes the waiter's, so age_flood = age_waiter + D. flood = legacyPriority(100)*300 + age = 30000 + age_waiter + D. waiter = 50*weightValue(400) + 10*weightUrgency(350) + StarvationRisk*weightStarvationRisk(500) + age = 23500 + 2500*(tick-1) + age_waiter. Decide's comparator at scheduler.go:156 gives a tie to the lexically smaller id and every flood id ('flood-NN') sorts before 'important', so the waiter must be STRICTLY greater: 2500*(tick-1) > 6500 + D. With StarvationBoundTicks = 5 that gives D <= 3499 (captureSpreadCeilingSeconds). The negative control's waiter scores a flat 23500 + age, so it stays behind the flood only while 23500 <= 30000 + D, i.e. D >= -6500 (captureSpreadFloorSeconds). The one-tick margin needs convergence by tick 4: 2500*3 = 7500 > 6500 + D, i.e. D <= 999 (captureSpreadMarginCeilingSeconds). The test recomputes the deficit (30000-23500 = 6500), the step (5*500 = 2500), the ceiling, the margin ceiling and the floor from priority.go's weights and scheduler.go's bound and fails if any declared constant disagrees; it also fails if StarvationBoundTicks is no longer 5, and asserts the fixtures' base age (100000 s) exceeds the largest tested |D| so ageSeconds' negative clamp never silently replaces the arithmetic.

checks.name: escalation-nothing-in-production-bounds-d
checks.summary: A9, RECORDED AND NOT FIXED. A Requirement's capture time is whatever instant its intake transaction happened at, and NOTHING IN PRODUCTION CONSTRAINS THE SPREAD between the capture times of competing Requirements: no clamp, no cap, no validation and no scheduling policy references it. A flood whose candidates were captured more than 3499 seconds (58 minutes 19 seconds) before the waiter therefore EXCEEDS the declared StarvationBoundTicks in a running system, and the D=+3500 case above measures exactly that at tick 6. Every available remedy -- raising the StarvationRisk step, normalizing or capping the age term, raising StarvationBoundTicks -- is a change to a scheduler decision rule, which V2-073's non_goal 3 forbids, and choosing among them means deciding what production should guarantee about capture-time spread. OWNER OF THE FOLLOW-UP DECISION: the tech_lead; V2-068, as the owner of the Snapshot builder, is where a chosen guarantee would be enforced. No assertion anywhere in this task was weakened, relaxed or reworded to make the limit disappear, and no number was adjusted to improve the appearance of the table. A further measured correction to the design packet is recorded in the mapping-rule check below.

checks.name: missing-capture-time-mapping-rule
checks.summary: A7, with the computed scores recorded. THE RULE: a Requirement with no recorded capture time is ordered as if captured at the snapshot's Now -- age zero -- never as an unbounded age. Half one, measured: a candidate at age zero ranked BELOW an otherwise identical candidate captured one hour earlier (recorded rank=0 score=18600 age=3600; age-zero-mapped rank=1 score=15000 age=0). The age-zero candidate deliberately carries the lexically SMALLER id ('aaa-missing' vs 'zzz-recorded'), so on a tie the comparator would have ranked it first; ranking the recorded one first is therefore a statement about the score, not about the ids. Half two, run explicitly as a POSITIVE CONTROL: a priority-ZERO candidate presented with the ZERO INSTANT scored 9223372036 (age 9223372036 seconds) and took rank 0, beating a priority-100 candidate scoring 33600 (age 3600 seconds). That is why the rule is age zero and not the zero instant: a missing value would otherwise become absolute precedence. MEASURED CORRECTION TO dp-v2-073 d6, recorded rather than glossed: d6 predicted 'roughly two thousand years expressed in seconds'. The measured magnitude is 9223372036 seconds, about 292 years, because time.Duration is an int64 of nanoseconds and now.Sub(time.Time{}) SATURATES at the maximum Duration instead of reaching year 1. The consequence d6 drew is unchanged -- 9223372036 dwarfs legacyScore's priority term, which is at most 30000 -- and that consequence is what the test asserts. The correction is written into the test file's own comment.
